key_insight: The paper introduces ERank, a simple label-free score that measures how visually rich an image is by counting how many independent channel directions it activates in a deep feature map. In practice, ERank can rank images from plain to complex using just one forward pass through a frozen pretrained encoder.
problem_solved: It addresses the lack of a fast, per-image, label-free measure of visual complexity and richness that works directly from image features rather than manual annotations or task-specific models.
method: Extract a deep feature map from a frozen pretrained encoder using a single forward pass.
Compute the channel covariance of the feature map and derive its effective rank (ERank) as a measure of how many decorrelated directions are activated.
Analyze ERank's behavior under noise and validate it against image properties such as codec bitrate, sharpness, and edge density.
impact: ERank gives practitioners a lightweight way to estimate image richness without labels or extra training. This can help with data filtering, quality assessment, dataset analysis, and building better image selection pipelines.

paper_title: ERank in Latent Space as an Image-Complexity and Richness Measure
paper_authors: Maksim Smirnov, Grigory Kononov, Anastasiia Linich, Egor Surkov, Egor Shvetsov
